Synopsis:
    Spring frosts and summer heatwaves have cut the 2026 Champagne grape harvest by roughly half versus the prior year, forcing producers to draw on reserve wines. Despite the shortfall, grape quality is described as exceptional due to ripeness and absence of mildew, though high alcohol levels pose winemaking challenges. The industry is already navigating structurally declining demand, economic uncertainty, and potential U.S. tariff headwinds.
